scope: Same original staged M128N96 kernel, fixed32tile, warm cache. Source-based mechanism comparison; observed model slope is diagnostic, not a new fitted parameter.

hlm_actual_path_composition.formula: phase1 + phase2 - phase0; these coefficients came from isolated physical paths, not full-GEMM timing.

cpp_source_rules.group_commit: After two returned sectors, a registered response owner directly commits32 halfword values to shared memory. No explicit per-warp LDG destination-register readiness or dependent STS issue path.
cpp_source_rules.compute: native40instruction per warp; matrix32/II8/pending2 and MOVM29/shared28 baseline unchanged.

phase_rule_screen.basis: Existing source-derived single-context warm all-hit phase graph; not newly calibrated from small runtime. Shared cache arbitration can perturb this by a few cycles.

cpp_source_rules.global_paths_not_intrinsic_latency: Four-cycle L2Slice hit eligibility is a behavioral cache-owner rule, not physical end-to-end global data readiness.
cpp_source_rules.stage_compute_overlap: Current SM controller serializes staging then compute for the same CTA. No claim of perfect inter-stage overlap; omitted physical load/store issue-readiness path is the capability gap.

conclusion: Most of the HLM-to-C++ stage-cost difference lies in the staging-path composition. The HLM retains an independently measured global-to-shared physical path; the C++ model substitutes sector-return/shared-commit state transitions. This locates a capability difference, not a uniquely identified physical delay or justification for installing the observed difference as latency.
limits: HLM physical phase coefficients include compiled issue/control/ownership/service effects.
C++ model phase screening and empirical model slope do not separately identify which omitted staging effect dominates.
Same large-hardware configuration used for both small shapes; no historical two-slot SV configuration conflation.
No new GPU run or model parameter adjustment.
